outcomes: Choose a decision-tree split using weighted Gini impurity
Build a random forest with row and per-node feature randomness
Fit squared-error gradient boosting to residuals
lessons: A tree partitions the feature space
Bag unstable trees into a random forest
Run the ensemble and inspect capacity

decision-tree.name: Decision tree
decision-tree.definition: A model that recursively partitions examples with feature threshold rules.
decision-tree.explanation: Each internal node tests one feature and sends a row left or right. Leaves return predictions from rows that reached them. Trees model nonlinear interactions without requiring feature scaling, but small data changes can alter early splits. Depth, leaf size, and pruning control whether a tree captures repeatable structure or memorizes training details. Evaluate every complexity choice on held-out data.

gini-impurity.name: Gini impurity
gini-impurity.definition: A measure of class mixing within a node.
gini-impurity.explanation: For binary positive fraction p, Gini is 2p(1-p). It is zero for a pure node and reaches 0.5 for an even split. Tree training compares candidate thresholds through the size-weighted impurity of their children. The measure guides training; it is not the model’s final held-out evaluation metric. Multiclass Gini subtracts every squared class proportion from one. Weight children by their row counts.

bagging.name: Bagging
bagging.definition: Training models on bootstrap samples and aggregating their predictions.
bagging.explanation: Each bootstrap sample draws the original number of rows with replacement, repeating some and omitting others. Independently fitted models see perturbed datasets. Voting or averaging can reduce variance when their errors are not perfectly correlated. Bagging does not remove bias from a flawed dataset, target, split, or feature pipeline. Out-of-bag rows can support an internal evaluation estimate. Keep bootstrap draws independent across models.

random-forest.name: Random forest
random-forest.definition: A bagged tree ensemble that also samples candidate features at each split.
random-forest.explanation: Every tree receives a bootstrap sample of rows. At every node, a fresh random subset of features competes for the split. These mechanisms create diverse trees, and their vote or average is usually steadier than one deep tree. Forest quality depends on useful individual trees whose errors are not too strongly correlated. The feature subset is redrawn independently at each node.

gradient-boosting.name: Gradient boosting
gradient-boosting.definition: Sequential additive modeling in which each learner reduces the current loss.
gradient-boosting.explanation: For squared-error regression, each new tree fits residuals left by the current ensemble. Its output is multiplied by a learning rate and added to the running prediction. Other losses use their negative gradients. Learning rate, tree depth, and number of rounds jointly control capacity, so validation must determine when additional learners stop helping. Sequential dependence distinguishes boosting from independently trained bagged trees.
